t: What k-d Tree Internals Is All About
title: What k-d Tree Internals Is All About
description: K-dimensional binary search: axis-aligned partitions for nearest neighbors.. This database covers k-d Tree Internals with full records: definitions, key facts, working procedures, and runnable demo programs, arranged on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. An index is a tradeoff: faster reads for slower writes and more space.
definition: k-d Tree Internals — K-dimensional binary search: axis-aligned partitions for nearest neighbors.
key_points: An index is a tradeoff: faster reads for slower writes and more space.
B-trees dominate because they balance read, write, and range scan performance.
LSM trees trade read amplification for write throughput; choose by workload.
The best index is the one your queries actually use; unused indexes are pure cost.
how_it_works: Identify the slow query with pg_stat_statements or the slow log.
Read its EXPLAIN plan; find the sequential scan or nested loop on large inputs.
Check the WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY columns; these are index candidates.
Design the index: equality columns first, then range, then sort; consider INCLUDE for covering.
Test with a hypothetical index or on a staging copy; verify the plan changes.
Build concurrently in production (CONCURRENTLY) to avoid locking writes.
Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that the index is used and the query is faster.
Monitor index size and write overhead; drop it if unused after a month.
